Subject: RE: Kickoff + a couple schema questions

Hi Olivia — great to meet you earlier. Looping in Marissa (CS lead) and Rishi (solutions) to jump in on the technical details.

High level answers:
1) Streaming + KV cache latency: with our default continuous batching and prefix caching we regularly hit ~600ms median p90 under typical production shapes. For guaranteed 1s median we recommend: 2 replica serving group, enable per-route low-latency policy, and a small autoscale headroom (burst + 20%). We'll add numbers from our benchmark doc.

2) Structured output schema: attaching waypoint-schema-v1.json — it includes the fields your QA asked for and an error taxonomy block (validation_error, runtime_error, partial_output). We recommend writing acceptance tests that assert presence/shape and that tooling-level errors map to validation_error.

3) Tool calling auth: short answer — our platform supports both mTLS endpoints (customer-managed certs on private deployments) and signed bearer tokens for hosted connectors. For Hub-style webhook partners we provide HMAC-signed payloads; for private connector endpoints we recommend mTLS when possible.

Action items:
- Marissa: share a concise runtime integration checklist and the implementation handoff spreadsheet.
- Rishi: provide an example tool-call auth flow and a minimal webhook example for Waypoint's team to exercise.

I'll set up a follow-up sync for next week (30 min).

Best,
Irene

Hi Olivia — hello from CS. I've put together a short implementation checklist (attached) and a suggested sprint plan you can drop into your tracker. Highlights:

- Sprint 0 (1 week): connectivity, sandbox model selection, key rotation, test harness for structured output
- Sprint 1 (2 weeks): streaming integration + KV cache tuning, add prefix caching, measure median/95th latency across representative traces
- Sprint 2 (2 weeks): tool-calling pilot (1 connector), auth validation, failure mode tests (simulate webhook 5xx and network latency)
- Sprint 3 (1 week): schema acceptance tests + rollout gating to prod

Implementation notes specific to Waypoint:
- Use per-route policy with low-latency goal and set max_tokens conservative for first 2 sprints
- Add an acceptance test that asserts JSON schema error taxonomy is mapped to HTTP 400 with body {"error_type":"validation_error"} when inputs break schema

Attachments: runtime-integration-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet with checklist + owners) and a short text file with sample test curl commands.

I'll be your primary CS contact during onboarding and will coordinate weekly checkpoints. If you'd like, we can make the first checkpoint a working session focused on the schema tests.

Hi Olivia — quick technical answers and an example flow.

1) Token -> mTLS migration: yes. The client-side integration is the same HTTP call shape (same endpoints, same JSON) — the transport-level auth changes. For hosted -> private you'll point to a different base URL and provide client certs instead of bearer tokens. We provide a consistent SDK config flag (auth.type = "token"|"mtls") so your code can switch with a config change. We recommend feature-flagging the switch during rollout.

2) Partial output streaming: when a model returns partial content we stream incremental JSON chunks with a top-level field "progressive": true. Example chunks:

{
  "progressive": true,
  "chunk_id": 1,
  "content": "{\"diagnosis\": \"possibility A\"}"
}

Final envelope when complete:

{
  "progressive": false,
  "chunk_id": 5,
  "content": "{\"diagnosis\": \"confirmed A\", \"confidence\": 0.92}",
  "error_type": null
}

This lets the UI render partial structured fields as they arrive and then reconcile on the final envelope. For error cases we use error_type = "partial_output" for expected truncation and include reason codes.

Attached are two snippets: toolcall-auth-examples.txt (HMAC example + SDK token rotation snippet) and a minimal curl example you can paste into your sandbox.

Let us know if you want us to join the 4/11 working session to walk through the stream traces live.
